Working with film-crew (single-shot mode), then banana-pro-director-2.0.

The workspace has no git repo and no NOTES.md, so I couldn't pull or check for open items. I didn't change any files, so I didn't add a notes entry.

**Assumptions** (non-interactive run):
- **Model and size:** Nano Banana Pro on Higgsfield, 16:9.
- **Season:** late November, to match today's date. That means brown-ochre slopes and first snow on the high ridges.
- **Company:** fictional, with no logos and no readable text, so no real mining company is shown.
- **Mine:** the pit is a generic Syunik-style terraced copper pit, not a recreation of a specific real mine.

**Crew pass (single shot)**
- **Director:** a quiet boardroom where decisions about moving a mountain get made. The pit outside the window is the silent subject. The room is empty, but someone has just used it.
- **Production design:** a renovated Soviet-era admin block, refitted around 2026.
  - Furniture: a long grey laminate table, mesh office chairs, a wall screen that is switched off, and a whiteboard with faded marker.
  - Mining props: a framed aerial photo of the pit, core-sample trays with greenish copper-ore glints, white hard hats and hi-vis vests by the door.
  - Signs of use: fine ochre blast dust in the corners of the window sill, and one half-finished paper cup of coffee (the human detail).
  - Text: anything written is unreadable.
- **People:** none.
- **DP:** a locked-off tripod at seated-to-standing eye height (about 140 cm), 24mm-equivalent lens, f/8 deep focus, three-quarter view down the table toward the window on the right.
  - Light: the window is the key light, and ceiling panels give a neutral fill.
  - Exposure: the brightest value is the overcast sky, held with detail. The darkest is under the table, with shadow detail kept.
  - Grade and grain: neutral, fine daylight grain.
  - Composite space: the near end of the table and chairs are left clear.

## FINAL

**Engine / mode:** Nano Banana Pro (Higgsfield), Mode 3B, environment plate with no people
**Settings:** aspect 16:9 · resolution 4K (2K for drafts) · references: none, text only · batch 4, then pick the cleanest plate

```
A still photograph captured on a locked-off tripod on a real location — a wide three-quarter view of an empty meeting room inside the administrative office of a copper mining company in the highlands of southern Armenia, 2026, the camera standing at the near end of a long conference table at about 140 cm height and looking down its length toward a large window on the right wall, the window filling the right-middle portion of the frame, the composition calm, level and observational, verticals kept straight, deep focus from the nearest chair back to the far mountains.

The room is a renovated Soviet-era office: smooth pale-grey painted walls, a suspended ceiling with flat square LED panels switched on at a neutral 4000K, light oak-effect vinyl flooring, white PVC double-glazed window frames with off-white vertical blinds drawn halfway open, a cast-iron radiator painted white beneath the sill. A long matte grey laminate table runs from the foreground toward the window, ten black mesh office chairs pushed in slightly unevenly, one chair turned out at an angle as if someone has just stood up. On the table: a few closed printed reports, two unlabelled glass bottles of mineral water and upturned glasses on a tray, a laptop closed and pushed aside, and one white paper cup of coffee left half full beside a torn sugar packet. On the left wall a large flat screen switched off and dark, below it a low cabinet holding two wooden core-sample trays of grey drill core with faint green and brassy metallic glints of copper ore. A whiteboard on the far wall carries erased marker ghosts and a hand-drawn bench diagram, faded and unreadable at this distance. A framed aerial photograph of the mine hangs near the door, and by the door three white hard hats sit on a shelf above hi-vis orange vests on hooks. Fine ochre dust settles in the corners of the window sill and along the radiator top, the only sign of blasting nearby. The near end of the table and the first chairs stay clear and uncluttered.

Through the window the open-pit copper mine fills the view: an enormous terraced pit cut into the mountainside in stepped benches, the rock in rust-ochre, grey, bruised violet and pale green-grey bands, switchback haul roads zigzagging down the walls, two tiny yellow haul trucks and a distant excavator giving scale, pale dust hanging low over the lower benches. Beyond the pit rise bare brown-ochre late-autumn highland ridges with the first thin snow on the highest peaks, their tops softened in low cloud. The view recedes in layers of atmospheric haze, colours desaturating toward the distance.

Flat overcast daylight from a uniform pale-grey sky is the key light, entering through the window and falling softly across the tabletop and chair backs, with the ceiling panels adding an even neutral fill. The brightest value is the cloud layer outside, held with visible texture; the darkest is the floor under the far end of the table, with detail kept in the shadows. Soft contact shadows sit under the chairs, beneath the cups and bottles, and where the cabinet meets the floor; a faint reflection of the room shows in the dark screen and the window glass. Exposure is balanced so interior and exterior both read clearly.

Captured with a wide-latitude cinema look through a 24mm-equivalent spherical lens stopped down to deep focus, natural perspective with minimal distortion, colour-negative daylight film rendition with fine 35mm grain across the whole frame — walls, laminate, rock, sky. Neutral naturalistic grade: cool grey daylight, honest rust and ochre in the mine, true whites on the frames and hard hats, shadows lifted gently and never crushed, highlights rolled off softly and never blown. Real photographic frame on a real camera, real lens, real painted walls, real laminate and real rock — no CGI, no rendered look, no digital cleanliness, no plastic surfaces, no AI smoothness, no teal-and-orange grade, no glow, no people, no logos, no readable text.
```

**QA note**
- **Framing:** 16:9, eye-height tripod, verticals straight, deep focus, clear foreground left for compositing actors.
- **Lighting:** sources are named (window key plus ceiling fill), the extremes are named, contact shadows are kept, and the window is not blown.
- **Realism and contradictions:** spherical lens and deep focus, with no anamorphic bokeh to fight the deep focus.
- **Rights:** no real company, brand, logo or person, and any text is unreadable.
- **For the composite:** keep this plate's 24mm lens, 140 cm height and window-from-the-right light direction when you shoot or generate the people.
- **If a generation fails:** if people appear, regenerate. If the window blows out to white, add "window exposure held, sky texture visible" at the start of the fourth paragraph.
